name: Mary McGuire (Mrs. Michael E. Riley)
bio: Daughter of Edward McGuire and Mary Jane Gaffney; age 12 in the 1870 Danville household. Married Michael E. Riley (1850-1892) and was widowed young; children Celia (1882-1938), Edward A. (1884-1907), James Aloysius (1885-1939), Johanna Gertrude (1886-1957), Mary A. (1888-1950, m. Daniel F. Burns) and Eugene Francis (1890-1918). Lived in Plymouth 1880-1940. name: Cecilia Marcella McGuire (Mrs. Murdock Dunn, later Mrs. Samuel Wilson)
bio: Daughter of Edward McGuire and Mary Jane Gaffney. Married Murdock "Murt" Dunn (b. 24 Dec 1862) at Plymouth, Pa., on 27 Dec [1886/87] (Luzerne licence 1790). The family emigrated to the Vancouver Island coalfield: in the 1901 Canadian census they were at South Wellington, Nanaimo, B.C. Murdock died in 1901; Cecilia remarried Samuel Wilson at Ladysmith in 1908 and died there in 1918. Children (FS): Thomas (1888-1937), Mary (1890-1935), Edward (1892-1909), Ellen (1894-1969), John Thomas (1897-1955), Murty Vincent (1902-1982). John's 3rd-great-grand-aunt.

name: Isaac Blydenburgh
bio: Miller of Smithtown, a 1798 partner in the Blydenburgh mill. Pelletreau's Blydenburgh genealogy traces him from Joseph Blydenburgh 1st and Deborah Smith (daughter of Jonathan, eldest son of Bull Smith) through Richard Blydenburgh 1st (1694-1772) and Benjamin. Path from Bull Smith: Jonathan -> Deborah -> Richard 1st -> Benjamin -> Isaac, 5 generations: 4th cousin 7 times removed. (Joseph 1st's later children by his second wife 'Collosia', including Joseph 1732-1833, are not Smith descendants.)

relationships.evidence: Descendant of Bull Smith via Jonathan Smith and Deborah (Smith) Blydenburgh; 4C7R to John

sources.citation: W. S. Pelletreau (ed.), Records of the Town of Smithtown (1898), Appendix (archive.org full text, scans recordsoftownofs00smitrich and recordstownsmit00pellgoog), App. pp. 483-486

name: Deliverance King
bioAdditions: Deliverance King, daughter of William and Dorothy (Hayne?) King, was baptized at Salem, Mass. ('1641:31:8') and was the first wife of John Tuthill (1635-1717) of Southold. She died at Southold aged 49 (the year is garbled in the OCR, but she died before John's second marriage on 28 May 1690). Akerly lists John Tuthill Jr. (b. 14 Feb 1658) among the children by this first wife. That makes her John Meier's direct ancestor, the mother of John Tuthill Jr., and she is missing from the tree (S1). Her father is probably the William Kinge of Salem (d. 1650) shown on WikiTree as Kinge-44.

Akerly lists John b. 14 Feb 1658 first among the 'issue, by 1st wife'

name: Henry James "Harry" Meier

burial.cemetery: Zachary Taylor National Cemetery, group burial, plot I 62-63, buried 15 Feb 1950

military.note: Staff Sergeant, U.S. Army Air Corps/Air Forces, WWII. Enlisted 27 Apr 1942 at Washington, DC (FS tree, from WWII Army enlistment records KMFG-KB8). Died 2 Jul 1943; group burial at Zachary Taylor National Cemetery, 15 Feb 1950. The 1946 Wilkes-Barre Record Almanac lists a 'Harry Meier' of Wilkes-Barre as missing.

bioAdditions: Harry Meier was the youngest son of Fred Aloysius Meier Sr. and Anna Mather, and a grandson of Henry J. Meier. He was a first cousin of John's grandfather James C. Meier. Born in Wilkes-Barre on 16 Aug 1923, he was with his father in the 1940 census (indexed 'Harry Meiers') and enlisted in Washington, DC, on 27 Apr 1942 (S1). He was a staff sergeant in the Army Air Forces. He died on 2 Jul 1943 in southern Italy; the FS tree gives Scorrano, Lecce. That was about a week before the Allied landings in Sicily, when U.S. heavy bombers were raiding airfields in Apulia, and the rank and 'group burial' suggest a bomber crewman lost with his aircraft. He was among the WWII dead brought home after the war and buried with his crew, as a group, at Zachary Taylor National Cemetery, Louisville, on 15 Feb 1950 (S2). He is very probably the 'Harry Meier, Wilkes-Barre, missing' of the 1946 Wilkes-Barre Record Almanac casualty list (S3), which earlier rounds could not place.

name: Christina Mayer
bioAdditions: Christina was born at Munzingen in May 1864. She was baptized as the illegitimate daughter of the single day labourer Paulina (Pauline) Mayer, who was herself the legitimate daughter of the citizen and master mason Heinrich Mayer and Juliana Senn. Her godparents were her uncle Friedrich Mayer, mason (John's 3rd great-grandfather, who emigrated to Hazleton in 1868), and her aunt Maria Anna Mayer, wife of the shoemaker Joseph Wenz (S1). That makes her a first cousin of Henry J. Meier. Her later life is unknown. The entry is No. 9 in the 1864 birth register, dated 16 May 1864; the exact day of birth in the text was read as the 15th, but that reading is uncertain.

name: Daniel Masse
bioAdditions: Daniel Masse was born on 29 Apr 1689 and baptized in May 1689 at the French Church of New York. His parents were Pierre Masse and Elisabet Mercereau, and his godparents were Daniel Mercereau and Marie Paré, wife of Ezéchiel Grazilier (S1). He was Jeanne Masse's elder brother. A Daniel Masse, almost certainly the same man since no other appears in the register, married Ester Fourret (also written Forrai). They had baptized there Pierre (b. 10 Dec 1712, bapt. 25 Dec 1712), Jean (b. 25 Apr 1716, bapt. 6 May 1716) and Ester (b. 21 Sep 1718, bapt. 28 Sep 1718); Ester's godmother was 'Jeane Masse', unmarried nine months before she married Daniel Lamoureux (S1). An Ester Masse, probably his wife, was godmother to Andre Lamoureux, son of Jeanne and Daniel, in Jan 1722 (S1).
